terms.comment: Safe from something is tūtus ab (ab hoste, Ov.). Also of a course that carries no risk: tūtum est with an infinitive, it is safe to (Quint. 9.2.66). In tūtō esse, to be in safety (Ter. Heaut. 4.3.30). Adverb tūtō, safely.

evidence: M-O s.v. safe (Tac. H. 4.20: innoxium iter)
terms.comment: Of a thing or an animal that does no harm. Also “innocent, guiltless” and, passively, “unharmed” (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: safe (of a place); classically, free from care
terms.comment: Classically free from care, untroubled (from sē- and cūra); “safe, secure” of a place is rare and later than Augustus (Lewis & Short). Prefer tūtus.

phrases.latin: quārē sollicitum potius aevum dūcitis quam rēgem mē creātis ictō foedere, quī vōs ab omnī tūtās praestem injūriā?
phrases.english: why spend your lives in fear rather than make a pact and choose me king, to keep you safe from all harm?
